run_mode: native venv, served (openai endpoint + `vllm bench serve`, random dataset)
gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97887 MiB, single GPU (sm_120 / cc 12.0, 188 SMs)
attention_backend: TRITON_ATTN (forced: Gemma4 has heterogeneous head dims head_dim=256/global_head_dim=512, FA4 unavailable) — same in all three configs
cuda_graphs: ON (not --enforce-eager); cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE; 'Graph capturing finished ... took 0.62-0.65 GiB' in every config
sanity: per-config chat gate ('What is the capital of France?' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.'); coherent in all three configs
schema: each config.results row = {input_len, ttft_ms, prefill_tok_s, tpot_ms, itl_ms, decode_tok_s}
prefill_tok_s_convention: DERIVED as input_len / (Mean_TTFT_ms/1000) by the harness. vLLM bench serve reports no standalone prefill throughput; TTFT includes prefill + the first decode token + scheduling, so this slightly UNDER-reports true prefill tok/s. Kept for consistency with the repo's other served vLLM files (same derivation).
notes: Reproduced with the repo harness perf-data/bench_vllm_cuda.sh, run from a scratch copy with ONE line changed: the hardcoded CUDA-12.8 PATH (line 58) replaced by PATH=/workspace/venvs/vllm/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH (venv bin first so flashinfer's ninja JIT is found; this box has no cuda-12.8). No other harness change.

The RTX 5090 run of this model (gemma4-12b-vllm-cuda-5090.json) REQUIRED VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 because that host had CUDA 12.8 (< 12.9) and flashinfer could not emit compute_120f. This box has nvcc 13.0, so the flashinfer sampler JIT works and the workaround is NOT needed — vLLM serves out of the box on sm_120 here.
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True set for all three configs (defensive against long-ctx fragmentation; 96 GB card has ample headroom regardless).

gpu-memory-utilization is CONSTANT at 0.90 across all three configs (unlike the 32 GB 5090 run which had to hand-tune bf16 to 0.92). On this 96 GB card bf16 weights (22.28 GiB ckpt) leave a 61.05 GiB / 1.67M-token KV pool at util 0.90 — 128k fits in every config, so this is a clean A/B.
DECODE metric = tpot_ms (== itl_ms at concurrency 1). Lower is better; this is the campaign target.

ctx=1024 ttft_ms carries first-shape warm-up (torch.compile specialization / cudagraph capture for the smallest bench shape); a chat warm-up request precedes the sweep but the 1024 point still sees some of it. Decode TPOT is unaffected. 4k+ TTFT is clean.

Every GPU-touching command ran inside `gpulease b1-12b ...`; one lease per config spanning serve -> sweep -> shutdown -> VRAM drain, exactly as the harness enforces. No server ever ran outside a lease.
NO OOM and NO failed points: all 3 configs x 7 contexts (1k..128k) completed.

configs.sanity_generated: The capital of France is Paris.
notes: bf16 reaches full 128k on this 96 GB card (KV pool 1,668,482 tokens >> 132,096). On the 32 GB 5090 bf16 OOMed past 16k — the card, not the model, was the limit there.

configs.config_desc: fp8 weight-only (--quantization fp8, dynamic e4m3 from the bf16 ckpt)
configs.sanity_generated: The capital of France is Paris.
notes: fp8 weights free ~10 GiB vs bf16 (available KV 61.05 -> 71.21 GiB); decode TPOT -30% to -37% vs bf16 across the ladder.

configs.config_desc: fp8 weights + fp8 KV cache (--quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8)
configs.sanity_generated: The capital of France is Paris.
notes: Same 71.21 GiB KV pool holds 3,892,361 tokens (exactly 2x fp8's 1,946,180) because fp8 KV halves bytes/token.

fp8kv's biggest win is long-ctx PREFILL/TTFT: at 128k TTFT is 8097 ms vs fp8's 15520 ms (-48%) and bf16's 16271 ms (-50%) — the fp8 KV path also speeds the attention over the growing cache. Decode TPOT is within ~1 ms of fp8 at short ctx and pulls ahead as ctx grows (128k: 17.30 vs 20.71 ms, -16% vs fp8).
